items.title: British Pound futures rally as Bank of England decision approaches.
items.excerpt: British Pound futures extended their advance for a sixth consecutive day, gaining 2.1% over the last 14 sessions as traders positioned ahead of the Bank of England's rate decision. Markets broadly anticipate the central bank to hike rates to 4%, with an additional 100 bps of increases priced in over the next year. Meanwhile, the U.S. Dollar Index traded lower following election results, as a divided Washington shifted the outlook for government spending and potential stimulus, weighing on Treasury yields and reducing the dollar's interest rate advantage.

items.title: Australian Dollar futures hit 2.5-week low after RBA rate hike.
items.excerpt: Australian Dollar futures fell for a second consecutive session, dropping 0.5% to 0.6960 and hitting a two-and-a-half-week low. The selling pressure follows the Reserve Bank of Australia's decision to raise interest rates by 25 basis points. Despite the hike, three dissenting officials voted to hold rates, and the central bank issued dovish forward guidance, pushing the Aussie dollar toward the lower end of its recent two-month range. Meanwhile, the broader FX market saw mixed action, with the euro and British pound trading slightly higher.

items.title: Euro FX futures rally on weaker dollar ahead of elections.
items.excerpt: Euro FX futures moved higher to start the week, reaching as high as 1.1237 before settling near 1.1200. The currency pair found support from a weaker U.S. dollar and rising uncertainty ahead of Tuesday's elections, bouncing off the year-to-date low set after the recent Federal Reserve meeting. Despite the price recovery, volatility increased, with the CVOL index moving higher on the back of broad market uncertainties. Meanwhile, speculators continued to build their net short positions, marking the largest short position for the group in over a decade.

items.excerpt: The trading week of November 2nd brings high-stakes midterm elections with all House seats and 35 Senate seats contested, while E-mini S P 500 options price elevated volatility. Simultaneously, the U.S. Treasury releases its quarterly refunding announcement, impacting 10-Year and 30-Year T-Note futures. Energy markets remain in focus as WTI crude oil futures hover near recent highs, leading into the October nonfarm payrolls report. Furthermore, a record-breaking corporate earnings slate features tech giants like Apple alongside hundreds of billion-dollar firms, complemented by critical central bank decisions from the RBA and Bank of England.

items.title: Japanese Yen futures pare gains as Bank of Japan holds rates.
items.excerpt: December Japanese Yen futures surrender overnight gains to trade slightly higher on the session, resuming a weekly decline of roughly 0.45%. The Bank of Japan holds its policy rate at 1.25% in an 8-to-1 vote, as underlying inflation hits the 2% target for the first time. Tokyo October headline inflation reaches 2.8%, above expectations, while September industrial production climbs 2.2% and unemployment falls to 2.4%.

items.title: British Pound futures rally as central bank divergence lifts prices.
items.excerpt: Dan Deming discusses the recent strength in British Pound futures as the contract trades higher for a second consecutive session. Deming highlights the growing policy divergence between major central banks, noting that the Federal Reserve's decision to hold rates steady has pressured U.S. yields and the dollar. In contrast, the Bank of England is expected to maintain a more hawkish stance, driving relative strength in the pound compared to other majors. He also analyzes the broader FX market and technical levels, observing that the pound is approaching the top of its one-month trading range near the 1.34 level.
items.author: CME Group

items.title: Strong U.S. data fuels rates.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino breaks down the morning's market action, noting stocks are mostly lower as Treasury yields fall across the curve, except for the 2-Year yield. Nasdaq futures lead the downside, while Russell futures manage a small gain. Iaccino highlights strong U.S. economic data, including third-quarter GDP at 3.4% and steady PCE inflation. This combination leaves little reason for the Fed to rule out another hike, keeping indices sensitive to yields. Geopolitics remain in focus as G24 foreign ministers meet in Atlanta, with the Strait of Hormuz and energy security on the agenda. Finally, earnings season rolls on with 133 large-cap companies scheduled to report.
